thread:
deploy-bot: :rocket: Deploy started: release/2026-03-15-87f3 (canary roll)

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Canary failures detected (5xx spike) — auto-create incident #INC-2026-3123. Paging oncall.

Elaine (oncall): Seeing canary error rate go from 0.2% -> 6.1% on /v1/generate, latency up ~300ms. Kicking off investigation.

Ryan (backend): I pushed the small router change in commit 87f3c1, it touched header normalization and a throttling flag. Rolling back now if needed.

Elaine (oncall): Quick triage: errors look like downstream model timeout 504 + some 500s from grpc proxy. Traffic split: 20% canary, 80% stable.

Luis (sre): Can we kill the feature flag for the new router? If flagkill reduces new path, we can stop canary without a full revert.

Ryan (backend): I can flip the flag. Flag name: feature.router_v2. Command: `/flag toggle feature.router_v2 off --env=prod`

Elaine (oncall): Go for it. Also annotate incident with customer impact. Sam, do we have any user-facing reports?

Sam (support): We've got two customers on support queue reporting increased latency and one timed-out ingest job. Priority B for now but could escalate. Not seeing broad errors in top 5 customers yet.

Ryan (backend): Flag toggled off at 3123456804. Confirming traffic 20%->0% to router_v2.

incident-bot: Feature flag change detected by Telemetry: feature.router_v2 set to OFF by Ryan. Canary traffic shifted back to stable set.

Elaine (oncall): Monitoring dashboards — error rate falling but still noisy. Latency returning to baseline after ~30s. I'm going to hold and run a quick post-deploy quick-revert if telemetry doesn't normalize in 5m.

Luis (sre): We should also prepare a single-commit revert just in case. Ryan, can you prepare the revert PR and keep it ready to merge? Use `git revert 87f3c1 --no-commit` then push branch `revert/router_v2-87f3c1`

Ryan (backend): Revert branch created and PR ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/8721 (WIP).

Elaine (oncall): Good. Telemetry shows errors stabilizing. I'm going to start an incident timeline and capture what we did: canary flagkill + prepared revert.

Product Ops: Notifying immediate affected teams and drafting a short customer note in case this gets wider. ETA on final status?

Elaine (oncall): Wait 10 more minutes, if everything stays green we'll close incident as mitigated and follow up with post-mortem.

(9m later)

incident-bot: Alert: error-rate back to baseline. No active pages for this incident in the last 3 minutes.

Elaine (oncall): Confirming metrics stable for 8m. No further customer escalations. We'll mark this mitigated. Action items: 1) Ryan to finish revert PR and keep it closed (not merged) for record. 2) Luis to run a canary replay test on staging. 3) Postmortem draft by Product Ops + SRE by EOD.

Ryan (backend): Revert PR closed as record (not merged), branch deleted. Command used: `git revert -m 1 87f3c1 && git push origin revert/router_v2-87f3c1`

Sam (support): Logged the customer report and sent an update that service is recovered.

Product Ops: Starting postmortem doc: https://redwood-internal/docs/incidents/INC-2026-3123. Will include timeline, root-cause hypothesis (header normalization + throttling edge case), and follow-up actions.

Elaine (oncall): Closing incident as mitigated at 3123456860. We avoided a full rollback thanks to the flag kill. Follow-ups as above — assign owners in the doc and schedule a 30m review tomorrow. :thumbsup:

Luis (sre): Suggestion for follow-up: add automated smoke checks for canary that check grpc proxy timeouts and the new header path within 60s of rollout.

Ryan (backend): Agreed. I'll add a checklist item to the release playbook and do a deeper review of the router change.

Sam (support): If anything else pops up, I'll re-open the incident. Thanks all. :pray:
